mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not higher when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 14% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: No negative returns when unemployment exceeds 14%.

mechanism_narrative: If unemployment rises while employment doesn't, it indicates economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns don't decrease when unemployment rises without employment growth.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher rates reduce borrowing, leading to lower S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Returns don't decrease during tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: Higher inflation erodes purchasing power, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns don't decrease with high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production signals reduced economic output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns don't decrease when production falls below 90.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts without retail sales growth indicates economic imbalance, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns don't increase with housing starts growth.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GDP growth in late expansion may not prevent market decline, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Returns don't decrease despite late-cycle GDP growth.
